title: Burning Number Conjecture
statement_text: For a connected graph $G$ of order $n$, $b(G) \leq \lceil \sqrt{n} \rceil$.
context_text: Introduced in [BJR16], the Burning Number Conjecture claims that paths achieve the largest burning number among all connected graphs of the same order. The conjecture remains open in general; it is known to hold for several special graph classes including spiders, caterpillars, lobsters, and graphs with minimum degree at least 23.
paper_contribution: Proves the best-known general upper bound $b(G) \leq \lceil\sqrt{4n/3}\rceil + 1$ for any connected graph $G$ of order $n$, establishes that the conjecture holds for all sufficiently large graphs with minimum degree at least 4, and shows it almost holds (off by at most 2) for graphs with minimum degree at least 3. Also proves the conjecture reduces to finitely many cases for trees of any fixed bounded growth.
paper_title: Improved pyrotechnics : Closer to the burning graph conjecture

title: Conjecture 7
statement_text: Let $T$ be a tree of growth $k$ and of order $n$. If $R$ is a finite set of integers such that $\{0, 1, \ldots, k\} \subseteq R$ and $\sum_{r \in R}(2r+1) \geq n$, then $T$ is $R$-burnable.
context_text: Graphs are finite, simple and undirected; $B(v,r)$ is the set of vertices at distance at most $r$ from $v$. In graph burning, in each round every unburned vertex with a burned neighbour becomes burned and then one new vertex is chosen to burn; the burning number $b(G)$ is the least $k$ such that all vertices are burned after $k$ rounds. The Burning Number Conjecture (BNC) states $b(G)\le\lceil\sqrt n\rceil$ for every connected graph of order $n$. Since the vertices burned after $p$ rounds are $\bigcup_i B(v_i,p-i)$, the BNC says that every connected $n$-vertex graph can be covered by balls of radii $0,1,\dots,\lceil\sqrt n\rceil-1$. For a finite set $\mathcal{R}=\{r_1,\dots,r_p\}$ of non-negative integers (a set, not a multiset), $G$ is $\mathcal{R}$-burnable if there are vertices $v_1,\dots,v_p$ with $\bigcup_i B(v_i,r_i)=V(G)$. The growth of a connected graph is the smallest $k$ such that every vertex is within distance $k$ of some path $P$ of the graph (trees of growth $k$ are $k$-caterpillars; it suffices to consider trees, via spanning trees). Since $\sum_{r=0}^{\lceil\sqrt n\rceil-1}(2r+1)=\lceil\sqrt n\rceil^2\ge n$, this conjecture strengthens the BNC for trees of growth $k$ whenever $\lceil\sqrt n\rceil-1\ge k$. The authors prove that $b(T)\le\sqrt{n+c_k}$ for trees of growth at most $k$, with $c_k$ depending only on $k$, so the BNC is asymptotically true for them and reduces to finitely many cases for each $k$, and they state that analogous arguments extend this to the present conjecture. They also prove $b(G)\le\sqrt{4n/3}+1$ for every connected graph.
paper_title: Improved pyrotechnics : Closer to the burning graph conjecture
